sam: hey team — Sam here (first day!). doing the runtime dev onboarding and hit a blocker when building from source inside our devcontainer. asking for a couple things: who to ping for access to the dev GPU pool, and any hints on the linker error below.

sam: docker build (using our devcontainer) fails at link stage:
```
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcublasLt
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
Makefile:212: recipe for target 'libredwood_runtime.so' failed
```
I'm using image `ubuntu:24.04` + CUDA toolkit installed via apt (.deb local repo). nvcc --version shows 12.2. I tried adding `/usr/local/cuda/lib64` to LD_LIBRARY_PATH in the Dockerfile but no luck.

leta: welcome Sam! :tada: for GPU pool access, ping `@infra` (they manage dev-gpu-pool). Also, where did you install CUDA from (runfile vs apt)? apt packages sometimes split cublas into separate packages.

ian: two quick checks:
1) inside the container, run `ls -la /usr/local/cuda/lib64 | grep cublas` and `ldconfig -p | grep cublas`
2) show your Dockerfile snippet where you set LD_LIBRARY_PATH and CUDA envs

evan: common gotcha: using a slim base image strips out symlinks that packages expect. If you installed CUDA toolkit via the package repo, make sure `cuda-cublas-12-2` (or matching version) is installed. If you're relying on host driver libs, you might need to mount them or use `nvidia/cuda:12.2-runtime` as base.

sam: here's the ls/ldconfig output I ran inside container:
```
$ ls -la /usr/local/cuda/lib64 | grep cublas
# no results

$ ldconfig -p | grep cublas
# no results

$ nvcc --version
Cuda compilation tools, release 12.2, V12.2.148
```
I did try symlinking a host lib (`/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so.12 -> /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcublasLt.so.12`) but that felt hacky and still failed at link.

natanael: do NOT symlink across distro libdirs if you can avoid it — can create ABI mismatches. Try installing the CUDA cublas packages inside the container:
```
apt-get update && apt-get install -y cuda-cublas-12-2 cuda-cupti-12-2
```
If you're using the NVIDIA apt repo, you might need to run `apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-12-2` which pulls the libs. Alternatively switch base image to `nvidia/cuda:12.2-devel-ubuntu24.04` — it has the dev libs in place.

sam: thanks. quick follow-up: where's the devcontainer repo for eng-runtime? I tried `git clone git@github.com:redwood/inference-devcontainer` but got 403. Who grants access?

leta: grant is via `@people-ops` + `@it`. ping `@alex` in infra; alex usually approves devcontainer and VPN access. also add yourself to the onboarding checklist: https://git.redwood.internal/onboarding/runtime-dev (has the devcontainer link).

ian: one more note for the build: our CMake looks for `cublasLt` via `find_library` expecting `-lcublasLt` to resolve. If you still hit link issues after installing packages, run `cmake -LAH` and check `CUBLAS_LIBRARIES` value.

buildbot: [CI] build queued for branch `sam/onboard` — job #4821.

sam: ok will try switching base image to `nvidia/cuda:12.2-devel-ubuntu24.04` and installing `cuda-cublas-12-2` in the Dockerfile. pinging `@alex` for access. I'll post results. thanks folks! :pray:

evan: lmk if you want me to pair on the Dockerfile for 15-20m. also drop a note in #devex for any doc gaps.

sam: updated — switching base image fixed the missing libs; build now gets further but hits a runtime symbol mismatch in tests (`undefined symbol: cublasLtMatmul`). will open another thread if I can't resolve. thanks all for the quick help! :rocket:
